title: queue-run output data
description: What the ledger holds after the enqueue — including on a replay.

path.description: Absolute path of the intake ledger the item lives on.
path.title: Path

item_id.description: The item's identity on the ledger — equal to the request_id (§10.S2). Every later transition record keys on this, and the current state of the item is the fold over its records.
item_id.title: Item Id

request_id.description: Echo of the client's idempotency token, so a relay can confirm the match.
request_id.title: Request Id

state.description: The item's state as written: always 'queued' on arrival. An item cannot ARRIVE placed — placement is a separate, disclosed decision.
state.title: State

replayed.description: True when this request_id was already on the ledger: NO line was written and ``record`` is the ORIGINAL item. The honest signal a relay needs — 'you already asked for this' is a different fact from 'I enqueued it', even though both are success.
replayed.title: Replayed

run_id.description: The item's COMPUTED run id when it could be derived at enqueue (§10.S2: '<run_name>-<cmd_sha[:8]>', a pure query, never minted); null otherwise. Two items with identical resolved params and the same run_name compute the SAME run_id — that collision is real and ``queue-status`` names it rather than silently collapsing the rows.
run_id.title: Run Id

enqueued_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC arrival stamp of the item (of the ORIGINAL item on a replay). §10.S3's accepted cost — trial params are chosen at enqueue — is why enqueue age is a fact worth surfacing.
enqueued_at.title: Enqueued At

queued_count.description: How many items on this ledger are currently in state 'queued' (after the append). The one number a relay can act on without a second call: it is the depth the next queue-advance will consider.
queued_count.title: Queued Count

record.description: The intake record as written (or as found, on a replay) — echoed so the session can relay exactly what the ledger now holds rather than a restatement of it.
record.title: Record
